changes_made.explanation: Normalized model names to standard capitalization (LLaMA-13B, Vicuna-13B). All existing items were correct and relevant.

Simplified ROUGE-L to ROUGE base form. Removed non-standard metrics that were implementation details rather than named evaluation metrics. Textual entailment was used as part of AutoAIS but is not a standard named metric itself. Answerability and ANLI were used internally but not as final evaluation metrics.
No LLMs were used as judges to evaluate the generated outputs. LLMs were only used as baseline generation models, not for evaluation.

guideline: Participants were asked to verify whether citations in generated summaries are correct by classifying each sentence as fully supported (FSupp), partially supported (PSupp), unsupported (NSupp), or contradictory (Contra) based on referenced passages
classifying each sentence as fully supported, partially supported, unsupported, or contradictory based on referenced passages
Annotators classified each sentence of the generated summary into one of four categories: Fully Supported, Partially Supported, Unsupported, or Contradictory.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into one clear statement. Normalized criteria to lowercase consistent format. Removed duplicate entries that represented the same criteria.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on text generation with attribution/citations, specifically query-focused summarization. The extraction was generally accurate but included some implementation details as metrics rather than the standardized evaluation metrics actually used. The paper conducts thorough automatic and human evaluations but does not use LLMs as judges.
